chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man forgets to wash his right hand, so he washes his left hand and wipes his head and his two feet, and then remembers, he should wash his right hand and his left hand, and wipe his head and his two feet; and if he only forgot his left hand, let him wash the left hand and not repeat over what he had already performed of ablution.
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Follow your ablution, part by part (sequentially).'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget to wash their right hand during wudu and continue with the rest of the ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'tartib' (sequential order) in wudu, distinguishing between a complete reset of the ritual when a major limb is missed versus a minor correction when only one hand is overlooked. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining the prescribed order of actions as a condition for validity, while offering practical leniency to prevent undue hardship during forgetfulness. The Imam’s instruction to 'follow your wudu with part of it' underscores the continuity required in ritual purity.
